newsitem.title: CHINA: China economic tsar says 1996 inflation 6.5 pct.
newsitem.headline: China economic tsar says 1996 inflation 6.5 pct.

text.p: China's economic tsar Zhu Rongji forecast that inflation would be below 6.5 percent in 1996, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
"It is possible to control it to six percent next year," Xinhua quoted Zhu as saying.
Consumer price inflation was 8.8 percent year-on-year in the January-September period.
Zhu, a vice-premier and member of the powerful seven-strong standing committee of the ruling Communist Party, forecast the economy would grow by about 10 percent this year, Xinhua said.
China's gross domestic product grew by 10.2 percent in 1995. GDP grew by 9.6 percent in January to September this year, the State Statistical Bureau said on Wednesday.
"The country's economy has developed in a sustained, rapid, healthy and stable way," Zhu was quoted as saying.
Zhu said China was expected to absorb $37 billion in foreign funds in 1996 compared with an annual average of $30 billion.
Planned free convertibility of the yuan on the current account would help to improve China's investment environment, Xinhua quoted the vice-premier as saying.
"It is totally unnecessary to worry about China's ability to make payments while doing business in China, and lending money to the country," Xinhua said. It gave no further details.
